biological_meaning: {response} varies normally around its expected value
Expected {response} is a linear combination of the mean-model predictors
Log residual SD of {response} is a linear combination of the scale-model predictors
Observations are conditionally independent given the predictors
Observations are conditionally independent given the predictors and the random effects
Residual SD is constrained positive via the log link
Observations are assumed not missing in a way that depends on the unobserved response
Each row of {response} is normal around its per-trait mean plus a contribution from the between-unit latent factors
Each trait has its own grand-mean intercept
Between-unit latent scores are independent standard normal
The loading matrix is parameterised lower-triangular with positive diagonal so it is identified up to sign
The between-unit T x T covariance is the latent product plus the diagonal of per-trait unique variances (\boldsymbol{\Psi}_B = 0 when no unique() term is present)
Row-level residual SD is constrained positive
Rows of {response} are conditionally independent given the latent scores
Observations are assumed not missing in a way that depends on the unobserved response
Within an observation, traits are conditionally independent given the latent scores, intercepts, loadings, and unique variances.
The loading matrix is identified up to rotation (and sign) of the latent axes. Interpret loadings only after a fixed rotation convention (e.g., lower-triangular, varimax).
Each latent axis can be flipped: sign of a column of {Lambda_B} and the corresponding column of {z_B} can both be reversed without changing the fit.
Missing trait values are assumed missing at random given the predictors and latent scores. Informative missingness violates this.

The implied between-unit trait covariance decomposes into a shared low-rank part (Lambda_B Lambda_B^T) and trait-specific unique variances (Psi_B). The interpretation is at the covariance level, not the per-observation level.
For gaussian traits, mu is on the identity (data) scale. Loadings interpret in the same units as the trait.
The two responses ({response_1}, {response_2}) jointly vary as a bivariate normal around their expected values with correlated residuals
Expected {response_1} is a linear combination of the first mean-model predictors
Expected {response_2} is a linear combination of the second mean-model predictors
Log residual SD of {response_1} is a linear combination of the first scale-model predictors
Log residual SD of {response_2} is a linear combination of the second scale-model predictors
Fisher-z transformed residual correlation between {response_1} and {response_2} is a linear combination of the correlation-model predictors
The residual correlation is constrained to (-1, 1) via the tanh inverse (atanh_guarded) link
The 2x2 residual covariance is built from the two SDs and their correlation
